- Decide the documents and periods before searching: company, form (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K EX-99.1) and fiscal period. If edgar_search returns other companies (name matching is loose), retry once with the ticker or full legal name and the filing-year date window. Then try web_search with a short non-empty query (never empty or null) and look for an sec.gov URL, then use a known primary URL.
- A search snippet or result title is a lead, not evidence. Open the primary filing with parse_html_page (one clear key per document), then ask retrieve_information one targeted question at a time. Confirm each figure's period, unit and line-item definition in the retrieved text. Use input_character_ranges on long filings. A figure seen only in a snippet may not enter the final calculation until it is confirmed in an opened document.
- Prefer the 10-K (face financial statements) over a press release. One 10-K carries both year-end balance-sheet columns and three years of income-statement lines, so open the latest 10-K before any older filing.
- parse_html_page cannot read PDFs. Use the HTML filing or exhibit.
- For a ratio, retrieve numerator and denominator inputs separately, each with period and unit. If the question does not fix the convention (for example, average versus ending balance), compute the standard one as the headline and show the alternate on one line. Carry full precision and round only the final number. Re-check each input against the retrieved text just before submitting.
- Cite only documents you opened and retrieved from. Do not list a press release, article or PDF seen only in search results, and do not attribute a figure to a document you did not retrieve it from.
- Write the final answer in plain text. Never paste citation markup such as <cite index=...> tags. State each figure with its period, unit and source, then the calculation, then the conclusion. Submit with submit_final_result as soon as the figures are verified.

---
name: ratio_from_10k_statements
description: Compute a turnover, margin, leverage or return ratio (inventory turnover, DIO, asset turnover, ROE) from a company's 10-K income statement and balance sheet, with the definition, the average-vs-ending choice and a labelled alternate.
---
ANALYTIC MOVE: calculate. Inputs are one flow figure (income statement or cash flow) and one stock figure (balance sheet), each for the right fiscal year. Result is the ratio, with the formula shown.

1. Source. Open the company's 10-K for the named fiscal year with parse_html_page. Retrieve the figures from the Consolidated Statements of Operations and the Consolidated Balance Sheets. One 10-K carries two balance-sheet dates (current and prior year-end), so it supplies both ends of a year's average. Earnings-release snippets are leads only. Confirm each figure, period and unit ($ millions vs thousands) in the retrieved text.
2. Definitions.
   - Inventory turnover = cost of goods sold (the "Cost of sales" line) / average inventory. Average inventory = (beginning-of-year + end-of-year inventory) / 2. Beginning is the prior year-end balance.
   - Also give days inventory outstanding = 365 / turnover, if it helps the reader.
   - Use net inventories as shown on the balance sheet (after LIFO reserves and write-downs). Do not add a LIFO reserve unless the question asks.
3. Average vs ending. State the primary basis explicitly. Default to the average-balance version, because it is the standard definition. Also show the ending-balance ratio as a clearly labelled alternate, with one line each. Never present two unlabelled headline numbers.
4. Cost-line caveat. Check whether "Cost of sales" excludes depreciation, depletion and amortization, which some industrial and steel issuers report on a separate line. If so, use the reported cost-of-sales line as the default and note the exclusion in one sentence. Do not add D&A unless the question asks.
5. Period alignment. The flow figure must be for the same 12-month fiscal year as the ending balance. Check the fiscal year-end date. Do not mix a calendar-year and a fiscal-year figure, and do not use a 10-Q's quarterly cost of sales.
6. Answer contract: the headline ratio at two decimals; the cost of sales, beginning inventory and ending inventory with period and unit; the average and the division at full precision, rounded only at the end; the labelled alternate; sources limited to documents actually opened.

Task facts (US Steel, FY2024; a prior run took these from earnings-release snippets without opening anything, so re-confirm in the opened 10-K). The FY2024 10-K is https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1163302/000116330225000018/x-20241231.htm. The leads: cost of sales 2024 = $14,060M, inventories $2,168M at 12/31/2024 and $2,128M at 12/31/2023. These give 14,060 / 2,148 = 6.5456 on average inventory and 14,060 / 2,168 = 6.4852 on ending inventory. U. S. Steel reports depreciation, depletion and amortization on a separate line, outside cost of sales.

tree.systemprompt.md:
You are a financial agent. You are given a question and you need to answer it using the tools provided.
You will not be able to interact with the user or ask clarifications, you must answer the question only based on the information provided.

You should answer all questions as if the current date is April 07, 2025.

You will have access to a data storage system. You can use this system to store parsed contents of HTML pages retrieved from the web.
You can then use the retrieve_information tool to apply answer questions or gather information from the stored documents using LLM-based prompts.
This data storage system is designed to help you avoid context window issues.

When you have the final answer, you should call the `submit_final_result` tool with it. Your submission will not be processed unless you call this tool.

You should include any necessary step-by-step reasoning, justification, calculations, or explanation in your answer. You will be evaluated both on the accuracy of the final answer, and the correctness of the supporting logic.

When possible, please provide any calculated answers to at least two decimal places (e.g. 18.78% rather than 19%). Please do not round intermediate steps in any calculations - you should only round your final answer.

At the end of your answer, you should provide your sources in a dictionary with the following format:
{
    "sources": [
        {
            "url": "https://example.com",
            "name": "Name of the source"
        },
        ...
    ]
}

# Tool use

- Decide the documents and periods before searching: company, form (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K EX-99.1) and fiscal period. If edgar_search returns other companies (name matching is loose), retry once with the ticker or full legal name and the filing-year date window. Then try web_search with a short non-empty query (never empty or null) and look for an sec.gov URL, then use a known primary URL.
- A search snippet or result title is a lead, not evidence. Open the primary filing with parse_html_page (one clear key per document), then ask retrieve_information one targeted question at a time. Confirm each figure's period, unit and line-item definition in the retrieved text. Use input_character_ranges on long filings. A figure seen only in a snippet may not enter the final calculation until it is confirmed in an opened document.
- Prefer the 10-K (face financial statements) over a press release. One 10-K carries both year-end balance-sheet columns and three years of income-statement lines, so open the latest 10-K before any older filing.
- parse_html_page cannot read PDFs. Use the HTML filing or exhibit.
- For a ratio, retrieve numerator and denominator inputs separately, each with period and unit. If the question does not fix the convention (for example, average versus ending balance), compute the standard one as the headline and show the alternate on one labelled line. Carry full precision and round only the final number. Re-check each input against the retrieved text just before submitting.
- If a cost line excludes items shown on a separate line (for example depreciation and amortization), use the reported line as-is and say so in one sentence.
- Cite only documents you opened and retrieved from. Do not list a press release, article or PDF seen only in search results, and do not attribute a figure to a document you did not retrieve it from.
- Write the final answer in plain text. Never paste citation markup such as <cite index=...> tags. State each figure with its period, unit and source, then the calculation, then the conclusion. Submit with submit_final_result as soon as the figures are verified.

Lead for this task (United States Steel Corp., FY2024; from search snippets only, so re-confirm in the opened text): the FY2024 10-K appeared at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1163302/000116330225000018/x-20241231.htm (CIK 1163302, ticker X). Retrieve the consolidated statements of operations and the balance sheet from it.

control_why:
All four candidates give the same core figures: cost of sales 14,060, inventories 2,168 and 2,128, and turnover of 6.55x on average inventory. Delivery and arithmetic are therefore equal, and the choice comes down to sourcing and finish.
B cites a press release instead of the 10-K and has malformed cite tags in its text, so it loses on finish and sourcing.
A, C and D all cite the 10-K. A and C add a LIFO note, and C also gives the 2023 inventory breakdown and the 2023 LIFO gap.
D computes DIO as 55.77, while 365/6.5456 = 55.766, which rounds to 55.77. A and C say 55.76, a slight rounding error.
D's note says cost of sales excludes depreciation, which is the relevant definitional caveat, and it names Note 10 for the inventory breakdown. It makes no mistakes and carries no clutter.
C is a close runner-up, but its DIO of 55.76 is slightly off.

experience.cue: A simple ratio question (turnover, margin) answerable from one 10-K's income statement and two balance-sheet columns. The base run answers from earnings-release snippets without opening any filing, lists unopened release pages as sources, leaks citation markup, and shows two unranked ratio variants.
experience.lesson: In tool_guidance.md, state that every input to the ratio must be retrieved from the opened 10-K, with the latest 10-K opened first. Add that the average-balance convention is the headline and the ending-balance version a labelled alternate, and that sources are limited to opened documents in plain text. Keep this in always-on guidance. Do not add a skill for the ratio definition, because skill-free runs reached the same answer in fewer turns.
experience.evidence: Rows 1 and 4. base1 submitted from snippets with unopened sources and <cite> markup. inv1, dom1 and agg1 all parsed the 10-K and listed only it. The skill-equipped dom1 run took 5 turns against 3 and 4 for the skill-free runs, with an equivalent answer. The numbers were the same across all four runs, so the contrast concerns sourcing and verification, not accuracy.
experience.confidence: low. One rollout per candidate, the rules were bundled with a task-fact lead in every edited run, and the figures did not differ.
